subject: research/osrobot-leannoise
professional: a senior human-robot interaction / assistive-feeding researcher with an estimation and control background (bite transfer, shared autonomy, human visuomotor models); first checks: does the 'perception delay' actually delay something that moves, are the delays in the human visuomotor range, does the human model make sense (involuntary sway vs voluntary lean), are the shares given with uncertainty, and is the result positioned against the bite-transfer literature.

evidence.correctness: Rerun: `PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 experiments/run.py` in a copy (16.0 s) gives a results.txt byte-identical to the committed one; figure.py regenerates bias_safe.svg byte-identical. Independent re-implementation from the README Method text and the stated constants, no subject import (`python3 -I /tmp/claude-0/audit-leannoise/scripts/indep.py`, 3.4 s): blind 100 mm/s lean at 0/10/20/40 mm misjudgement gives fed 1.00/0.91/0.70/0.50, safe 1.00/0.83/0.60/0.47 (README match); camera 20 mm 0.78; blind delay 0.5/1.0 s safe 0.95/0.46; camera delay 1.0 s 0.91; passive 0.21 and 0.71; 50 mm/s 0.69 (138/200), all equal to results.txt and to osrobot-lean's results.txt rows. Analytic check: every failed blind feed has |bias| > R_MOUTH (min 12.5, 14.8, 14.9 mm), and fed >= P(|N(0,sigma)| <= 12 mm) = 0.770/0.451/0.236, consistent. But the delay sweep does not measure what it is said to: the blind arm's spoon is stationary at y = 0 once its lateral transient ends (about 0.2 s, before the lean starts at about 0.3 s), so a late view of it is harmless; the drop at 0.5 and 1.0 s comes from model.py:61 clamping the history index to ylog[0], the tip's start position (which run_trial sets to the mouth's t = 0 sway position, model.py:48). Probe (`python3 -I scripts/probe.py`): 25% and 90% of lean steps read that clamped pre-start entry at 0.5 and 1.0 s delay, and if the tip simply starts at y = 0 the blind safe share is 1.00 at every delay. The numbers are reproduced; the delay effect is a start-condition artifact.
evidence.completeness: Claimed and checked: 4 tests under a second (4 OK in 0.32 s); run.py about 15 s (16.0 s, writes results.txt identical); figure.py writes bias_safe.svg from results.txt (identical, needs research/_shared/linefig.py); every number in the five README bullets is in results.txt; live page https://marisstella.app/research/osrobot-leannoise/ returns 200 and its summary numbers (0.60 vs 0.78, 0.83/0.60/0.47, 0.50 fed, 1.0 s -> 0.46) match results.txt. No stubs or TODOs. Swept grid matches the Method section (4 delays x 4 biases x 2 leans x 2 arms, 200 seeds).
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 4 tests OK, 0.32 s. No test pins a number: test 1 (tests/test_model.py:6-9) compares run_trial with defaults to run_trial with explicit zeros, i.e. the function with itself, so it does not check the README's 'reproduces osrobot-lean, and a test checks it'. Four mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: delay ignored (model.py:61, int(round(perc_delay/DT)) -> 0) SURVIVED; misjudgement std divided by 4 (model.py:44) SURVIVED; lean gain halved (model.py:63) SURVIVED; perceived position replaced by true tip (model.py:61) caught by test_bias_hurts_blind_arm_feeding. Three of four core mutants survive, including the one that deletes the delay feature the project is about.
evidence.craft: Read model.py, run.py, figure.py, tests/test_model.py, pyproject.toml, and diffed model.py against research/osrobot-lean (8 changed lines). Small and readable, seeded and paired correctly (separate RNG stream for the bias, seed + 10**6). Defects: the whole engine is a fourth copy (osrobot-assist -> lean -> leannoise -> leanshrink) rather than an import; summarise() (model.py:98) cannot pass lean/delay/bias and is dead, while run.py:10-14 re-implements the summary inline; history clamp at model.py:61 silently invents a pre-start past; run.py is a flat script with no functions, so the table logic is untestable; ylog grows without bound (harmless at 6,000 steps).
evidence.claims: Disclaimer and limits are good: README.md:3 says every constant is assumed, nothing built or tested, AI-assisted, not affiliated with CAIRO Lab; the Limitations list the constant offset, pure lag, unlimited chase and the unsourced 2 N limit. Misjudgement bullets (README.md:9-11) are backed by results.txt and recompute. Not backed: README.md:12 attributes the delay effect to 'a large part of the sway period' and the conclusion README.md:13 says the camera can be dropped only if the person is 'not more than about half a second late', both resting on the start-pose artifact above; README.md:14 'a test checks it' (no test compares to osrobot-lean or pins 0.69); README.md:13 calls 12 mm 'the mouth opening' while model.py:14 defines R_MOUTH as the half-width (opening 24 mm). research/README.md:646 and the live page repeat '1.0 s drops the blind arm to 0.46' as a perception-delay finding.
evidence.fitness: Job: a feeding-robot researcher deciding whether user anticipation can replace mouth tracking under realistic human perception. The misjudgement sweep is a clear, reproducible toy result and osrobot-leanshrink already builds on it. But nearest prior work is not engaged: the bite-transfer literature (Gallenberger et al. 2019, HRI, 'Transfer depends on acquisition'; Belkhale et al. 2022, ICRA, bite transfer balancing efficiency and comfort; Jenamani et al. 2024, HRI, 'Feel the Bite' inside-mouth transfer with mouth perception) studies exactly how head motion and utensil meet, and shared-autonomy work (Javdani et al. 2018, IJRR) models human intent noise; none is cited. All constants are assumed, no intervals are given on 200-trial shares (binomial SE about 0.035 at 0.6), and the delay half of the result is an artifact. Novelty: an incremental parameter sweep on an in-repo stylised model; not something a researcher could cite as a finding about people.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard human visuomotor modelling and HRI practice: (1) the human's lean controller subtracts the exact current head sway base(t) (model.py:62), so the person perfectly cancels their own involuntary sway with zero delay while seeing the spoon late; delay is applied only to a stationary object. (2) Human visuomotor latency is about 0.1-0.3 s; in that range the model shows no effect by construction, and the effects at 0.5-1.0 s are from the clamp. (3) A misjudged feed keeps pressing on the lip for up to 12 s (T_MAX) with no retreat; a practitioner would cap contact time, which also inflates 'touch' and peak counts. (4) The 2 N comfort limit and the Hunt-Crossley parameters are unsourced (stated). (5) No confidence intervals or paired test on 200-trial proportions. A senior HRI reviewer would accept the misjudgement mechanism as a qualitative point and reject the delay conclusion.

defects.what: The blind-arm 'perception delay' result is a start-condition artifact: the spoon is stationary during the lean, so a late view of it is harmless; the drop to 0.95 / 0.46 safe at 0.5 / 1.0 s comes from the history index being clamped to ylog[0], the tip's start position (set to the mouth's t = 0 sway position). With the tip starting at y = 0 the blind arm is 1.00 safe at every delay. README.md:12-13, research/README.md:646 and the live page present it as a delay effect and the conclusion's 'not more than about half a second late' rests on it.
README says 'a test checks' that zero-error rows reproduce osrobot-lean; the test compares run_trial with defaults to run_trial with explicit zeros (the same code path) and pins no number.
No test pins any output; 3 of 4 core mutants survive, including deleting the perception delay entirely.

Human model: the lean controller subtracts the exact current head sway base(t), so the user cancels their own involuntary sway instantly while only the (stationary) spoon is seen late; delays swept (0.5-1.0 s) are outside human visuomotor latency (about 0.1-0.3 s), where the model shows no effect by construction.

Nearest prior work (robot-assisted bite transfer: Gallenberger et al. 2019 HRI, Belkhale et al. 2022 ICRA, Jenamani et al. 2024 HRI; shared autonomy, Javdani et al. 2018 IJRR) not cited; no confidence intervals or paired test on 200-trial shares.
Conclusion calls 12 mm 'the mouth opening'; R_MOUTH is the half-width (opening 24 mm).
summarise() cannot pass lean/delay/bias and is unused; run.py re-implements the summary inline; the engine is a fourth copied file in the osrobot-lean* chain.
A misjudged feed presses on the lip for up to T_MAX = 12 s with no retreat, inflating touch and peak force for failed feeds (limitation is mentioned but not bounded).

verdict: Reproducible and honestly disclaimed: the rerun and an independent re-implementation give byte-identical tables, and the misjudgement result (a constant offset beyond the 12 mm half-width leaves the blind arm unable to feed, 0.83/0.60/0.47 safe) checks out analytically. But half the headline is an artifact: the blind arm's spoon is stationary while the user leans, so the 'delay' effect at 0.5 and 1.0 s comes only from the history clamp at model.py:61 reading the tip's start pose; with a neutral start the blind arm is 1.00 safe at every delay, so the conclusion's 'not more than about half a second late' is unsupported. Tests pin no number (3 of 4 mutants survive, including removing the delay), the README's 'a test checks it' is a self-comparison, the human model cancels its own sway perfectly, and the bite-transfer literature is not cited. Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 1).
